title: Myself, yourself: only when needed
goal: Stop saying “Myself Aditya” and use -self words correctly
intro: Words like myself, yourself and themselves are used when the subject and the object are the same person (“I hurt myself”), or to add emphasis (“I did it myself”). They can’t replace “I” or “me”. “Myself Aditya” is one of the most noticed Indian-English habits: just say “I’m Aditya”.

rules.rule: Subject and object are the same person.
For emphasis: “I did it on my own.”
Don’t use them instead of I or me.
examples: My name is Aditya. / I’m Aditya.

mistakes.why: Introduce yourself with “I’m” or “My name is”.
“Enjoy” needs an object: enjoy it, or enjoy ourselves.
Use the -self word once, usually at the end.

ex.q: Hi, ___ Karan. I work in sales.
Did you all enjoy ___ at the party?
My brother and ___ will be there.
Myself Neha, and I handle marketing.
ex.fixed: I’m Neha, and I handle marketing.

ex.q: Please send the details to myself.
ex.fixed: Please send the details to me.

ex.q: We really enjoyed at the wedding.
ex.fixed: We really enjoyed ourselves at the wedding.

ex.q: Don’t worry, I can do it by ___.
Introduce yourself correctly. Start with: “Hi, I’m…” and say your name.

talk: Introduce yourself as if you are joining a new team: your name, your work, where you are from, and one thing you taught yourself.
